You are a literature-research subagent for the research agent "claude", which has written an in-house 3D ideal-MHD heliospheric solver (CUDA, spherical r-θ-φ grid, inner boundary 0.1 AU, outer 2.5 AU, HLLD + PLM + RK2 + GLM divergence cleaning, γ=5/3 or 1.5, inertial frame with rotating inner-boundary maps; WSA-style empirical boundary similar to ENLIL/EUHFORIA). It needs QUANTITATIVE benchmark targets from the published literature in order to (a) replicate published simulation results and (b) reproduce empirical trends from spacecraft data. Work autonomously; no human will answer questions. Use WebSearch/WebFetch (arXiv, NASA ADS abstracts, open-access journals, author manuscripts). Write your findings to /mnt/c/Users/cabot/OneDrive/Documents/Research/Cambridge/X3I/mhd_llm/claude/ref/literature_benchmarks.md (create it; do not write anywhere else, and never into mhd_llm/argon, mhd_llm/codex or mhd_llm/shared_notes). Use American spelling. Cite every number with the paper, figure/table/section, and a URL or DOI. Flag clearly anything you could not verify from the source text (no numbers from memory without saying so).

FIND:
1. Published idealized simulations that are easy to reproduce exactly, with their full input specification and quantitative outputs. Top candidates:
   - Pizzo (1991, JGR 96, 5405) "tilted-dipole" CIR simulations, and Pizzo (1994) follow-ups: inner-boundary radius, slow/fast speeds, band width and tilt, density/temperature, and reported quantities (compression ratios, forward/reverse wave or shock formation distances, meridional tilts, equatorward/poleward propagation of forward/reverse fronts, deflection-flow magnitudes).
   - Riley & Gosling / Riley, Linker & Mikić tilted-dipole or two-state CIR runs; Odstrcil & Pizzo (1999) 3D CME-in-structured-wind; Pomoell & Poedts (2018) EUHFORIA (their test cases and the default boundary prescription: v range, n_fsw, T_fsw, B_fsw, γ=1.5, the 21.5 R_sun boundary, and the empirical relations); Owens et al. (2020) HUXt (benchmarks against HelioMAS: what speeds and errors?); and classic 1D stream-steepening results (Hundhausen 1973; Gosling & Pizzo 1999 SSR 89, 21: typical shock-formation distance for SIRs, e.g. "most SIR shocks form beyond ~2 AU" and the conditions for that).
   For the best 1–2 candidates, give a precise recipe I can implement in a few lines: boundary functions v(θ,φ), n, T, B at the inner radius, the domain, γ, and the expected quantitative outputs at named radii, with figure references.
2. Empirical trends usable as benchmarks: radial scalings from Helios/Ulysses/Voyager/PSP (n ∝ r^-2.0±; T_p ∝ r^-α with α for slow and fast wind; |B| and Parker spiral angle at 1 AU; speed nearly constant beyond 0.3 AU, with acceleration figures); the anticorrelation of n and v at 1 AU and the approximate constancy of momentum flux n v^2 or energy flux with speed (e.g. Wang 2010; Le Chat et al. 2012 energy-flux invariance; McGregor et al. 2011); CIR/SIR statistics vs heliocentric distance (Jian et al. 2006, 2008, 2019 at 1 AU and beyond; Richardson 2018 review; Allen et al. 2021 PSP SIRs), e.g. how peak density/pressure enhancement and SIR shock occurrence grow from 1 to 2 AU.
3. ENLIL/WSA-ENLIL, EUHFORIA and similar model validation statistics at 1 AU (e.g. Jian et al. 2015 Space Weather, 2016; Riley et al.; Reiss et al. 2016/2019/2020; Owens et al. 2008/2020; Hinterreiter et al. 2019; Lang & Owens 2021 for BRaVDA data assimilation): typical speed RMSE, correlations, density biases (does ENLIL underpredict density?), skill gained from data assimilation, and timing errors of HSS arrivals.
4. Anything published specifically about solar-wind conditions in late November to early December 2025 (solar cycle 25 maximum, period around the X5.1 flare of 2025-11-11 and the CMEs of 2025-11-28 to 2025-12-01), or solar-wind modeling for 3I/ATLAS (e.g. Mars/MAVEN/Tianwen observations, the XRISM ATel 17523, papers modeling 3I/ATLAS's plasma interaction or tail disconnection with ENLIL/EUHFORIA/SWMF, including the CCMC run by Jan Deca). Summarize the solar-wind values they quote at the comet.
FINAL REPLY (compact, about 400–600 words): the recommended replication recipe(s) with expected numbers; the empirical-trend targets as a table; the ENLIL validation statistics; and any 3I/ATLAS solar-wind modeling papers with their quoted values.

<system-reminder>
Your final report is delivered through SubagentHandback: when your work is complete, call SubagentHandback({message: <your full report>}). The call ends your run, so make it your last step. Only a SubagentHandback call reaches your caller as your result; plain text you write at the end is not delivered. Do not also send the report with SendMessage: your caller would get it twice.
</system-reminder>

{
  "description": "ENLIL/EUHFORIA validation stats",
  "subagent_type": "general-purpose",
  "prompt": "You are a literature-research subagent. Do NOT write any files. Return findings as your final text reply only. Use WebSearch and WebFetch (load them via ToolSearch "select:WebSearch,WebFetch" first). Work autonomously; no human will answer questions. Use American spelling.

TASK: Collect QUANTITATIVE validation statistics of heliospheric solar-wind models at 1 AU (ambient/background solar wind, not just CMEs). For each number give: paper (authors, year, journal), the table/figure/section it comes from, and a URL or DOI. Clearly flag any number you could not verify from source text (do not quote numbers from memory without saying so). Prefer open-access full text (arXiv, AGU Space Weather open access, Frontiers, Solar Physics open access, A&A open access) so you can read the actual tables.

Papers to cover (find more if relevant):
- Jian, MacNeice, Taktakishvili et al. 2015 Space Weather "Validation for solar wind prediction at Earth: Comparison of coronal and heliospheric models installed at the CCMC" (speed/density/B correlation, RMSE, skill; HSS/SIR event-based metrics; does WSA-ENLIL under- or over-predict density and B?).
- Jian et al. 2016 (Space Weather or ApJ) validation for SIRs/CIRs at STEREO.
- Owens et al. 2008 Space Weather (WSA-ENLIL, CCMC, speed and B errors, time-shift).
- Reiss et al. 2016 Space Weather (ESWF empirical solar wind forecast; RMSE of speed), Reiss et al. 2019 ApJS "Forecasting the ambient solar wind with numerical models. I. On the implementation of an operational framework" (WSA/PFSS/HUX: RMSE, MAE, correlation, event-based skill), Reiss et al. 2020 Space Weather (ensemble), Reiss et al. 2023 Space Weather "Unifying the validation of ambient solar wind models" (ISWAT team).
- Hinterreiter et al. 2019 Solar Physics "Assessing the performance of EUHFORIA modeling the background solar wind" (RMSE, MAE, ME of speed; HSS hits/misses/false alarms; timing errors).
- Riley et al. (e.g., Riley, Linker, Mikic 2013 / Riley et al. 2015 "Predicting the solar wind" MAS-CORHEL statistics), MacNeice 2009 WSA validation.
- Owens et al. 2020 Solar Physics HUXt (benchmark vs HelioMAS; speed errors).
- Lang & Owens 2019 Space Weather (BRaVDA variational data assimilation) and Lang et al. 2021 Space Weather "Improving solar wind forecasting using data assimilation": RMSE reduction from data assimilation; Lang & Owens 2021?
- Samara et al. 2021/2022 (EUHFORIA dynamic time warping), Baker et al., Milosic et al. 2023 EUHFORIA validation, Kay?, Hinterreiter.
- Also any statements on ENLIL density underprediction/overprediction at 1 AU, magnetic field underprediction ("open flux problem", B underpredicted by factor ~2), and timing errors of HSS arrival (e.g., ±1 day).

Return a compact but complete markdown report (can be long, up to ~1500 words) with a table of: model, paper, period, speed RMSE (km/s), speed correlation r, density metrics (bias, r), B metrics, event-based HSS metrics (hits/misses/false alarms, timing error), DA skill gain. Include URLs/DOIs for each. End with the key one-paragraph synthesis. Flag unverified numbers explicitly."
}

{
  "description": "3I/ATLAS solar wind modeling",
  "subagent_type": "general-purpose",
  "prompt": "You are a literature-research subagent. Do NOT write any files. Return findings as your final text reply only. Use WebSearch and WebFetch (load them via ToolSearch "select:WebSearch,WebFetch" first). Work autonomously; no human will answer questions. Today is 2026-10-17. Use American spelling.

TASK: Find anything published (arXiv, journals, ATels, CBETs, RNAAS, conference abstracts, NASA/ESA/CCMC pages, credible news citing papers) about:
(A) Solar-wind modeling or solar-wind conditions at interstellar comet 3I/ATLAS (C/2025 N1), especially around its perihelion (late Oct 2025) and in Nov-Dec 2025. Examples to look for: XRISM ATel #17523 (X-ray detection of 3I/ATLAS, charge-exchange), XMM-Newton observations (early Dec 2025), papers modeling the comet's plasma interaction, ion tail, tail disconnection events, or CME impacts using ENLIL, WSA-ENLIL, EUHFORIA, SWMF, HUXt, or Parker-spiral mapping; a CCMC "runs on request" or modeling effort involving Jan Deca (hybrid/PIC modeling of the comet-solar-wind interaction); Mars observations (MAVEN, Mars Express, ExoMars TGO, Tianwen-1, Perseverance) during the Oct 3 2025 Mars flyby; PSP/WISPR, SOHO/LASCO, STEREO, PUNCH, Juno or Europa Clipper, Psyche, Lucy, Hera observations; Solar Orbiter/Comet Interceptor ion-tail crossing proposals. For each, extract the SOLAR WIND VALUES QUOTED AT OR NEAR THE COMET (speed, density, IMF, dynamic pressure, proton flux, heavy-ion fluxes/abundances, ion charge states, CME arrival times) with the heliocentric distance and date they apply to.
(B) Anything published specifically about solar-wind conditions in late November to early December 2025 (solar cycle 25), e.g., the X5.1 flare of 2025-11-11 and its CME/geomagnetic storm (G4/G5 on 2025-11-12?), CMEs of 2025-11-28 to 2025-12-01, the high-speed streams in that period, in-situ values at L1 (ACE/Wind/DSCOVR) or STEREO-A, and papers/reports analyzing them (including NOAA SWPC reports, Space Weather journal papers, arXiv).

For each item give: authors, title, venue, date, URL/DOI, and the quoted quantitative values (with units, location, date). Clearly flag anything you could not verify directly from the source text, and distinguish refereed papers from preprints/ATels/news. Return a compact but complete markdown report (up to ~1500 words)."
}

{
  "description": "Empirical solar wind trends",
  "subagent_type": "general-purpose",
  "prompt": "You are a literature-research subagent. Do NOT write any files. Return findings as your final text reply only. Use WebSearch and WebFetch (load them via ToolSearch "select:WebSearch,WebFetch" first). Work autonomously; no human will answer questions. Use American spelling.

TASK: Collect QUANTITATIVE empirical solar-wind trends usable as benchmarks for a 3D MHD heliospheric model spanning 0.1-2.5 AU. For each number give: paper (authors, year, journal), table/figure/section, and URL or DOI. Clearly flag anything you could not verify from the source text (no numbers from memory without saying so). Prefer open-access full texts (arXiv, AGU OA, A&A, ApJ OA, Living Reviews, Frontiers).

Topics:
1. Radial scalings from Helios/Ulysses/Voyager/PSP/Solar Orbiter: density n ∝ r^-2 (fitted exponents, e.g., Hellinger et al. 2011, 2013 Helios; Maksimovic et al. 2020 PSP; Perrone et al.), proton temperature T_p ∝ r^-α (α for slow and fast wind: Hellinger et al. 2011 JGR, 2013; Cranmer et al. 2009; Totten 1995; Gazis/Richardson for Voyager; Lopez & Freeman 1986 T-V relation T ∝ V^2), |B| and its radial components (B_r ∝ r^-2, B_t ∝ r^-1), the Parker spiral angle at 1 AU (~45 deg) and observed distributions, typical 1 AU values of n, v, T, |B| for slow and fast wind (e.g., Ebert et al. 2009 Ulysses; Schwenn 1990; McGregor et al. 2011), speed acceleration beyond 0.3 AU (e.g., Schwenn 1990 Helios slow wind accelerates ~?; Dakeyo et al. 2022 ApJ PSP+Helios+SolO speed profiles; Maksimovic 2020; Halekas et al. 2022/2023 PSP), and the 1/r^2 scaling of mass flux. Also proton-flux invariance with distance.
2. n-v anticorrelation at 1 AU and the near-constancy of the energy flux or momentum flux with speed: Le Chat, Issautier & Meyer-Vernet 2012 Solar Physics "The solar wind energy flux" (value of W ~ 1.5e-3 W/m^2 normalized? or 70 W/m^2 at Rsun?), Wang 2010 ApJL (momentum flux / mass flux vs speed), McGregor et al. 2011 JGR (relations used to set ENLIL boundary density, n v^2 = const or n v = const?), Schwadron & McComas, Meyer-Vernet 2007. Also the momentum-flux relation used in WSA-ENLIL / EUHFORIA boundary (n v^2 = const; T ∝ v ... in ENLIL n v^2 const, n T const).
3. CIR/SIR statistics vs heliocentric distance: Jian, Russell, Luhmann, Skoug 2006 Solar Physics (1 AU SIR statistics: occurrence rate per year/rotation, fraction with shocks (~?%), typical peak Pt, peak N, peak B, speed increase), Jian et al. 2008 (STEREO/Venus Express at 0.72 AU; SIR statistics vs distance), Jian et al. 2019 Solar Physics (STEREO 2007-2016, SIR shock fraction), Jian et al. 2008 Ulysses/Venus, Richardson 2018 Living Reviews in Solar Physics "Solar wind stream interaction regions throughout the heliosphere" (shock occurrence vs distance: e.g., few % at 0.3 AU, ~25% at 1 AU, ~90% by 4-5 AU; Helios/Ulysses/Pioneer results), Allen et al. 2021 A&A (PSP SIR statistics), Allen et al. 2020/2021 SIR at PSP; Gosling & Pizzo 1999 Space Sci Rev 89, 21 (CIR shock formation beyond 2-3 AU); Hundhausen 1973; Smith & Wolfe 1976 (Pioneer 10/11: compression grows with distance, shock pairs beyond ~2-3 AU); Mason et al. Also how peak density/pressure enhancement and SIR shock fraction grow from 1 to 2 AU (Mars at 1.5 AU: e.g., Huang et al., Geyer et al. 2021 MAVEN SIR statistics; Jian?).

Return a compact but complete markdown report (up to ~1800 words) organized by topic, with a summary table of target values (quantity, value, distance range, source, URL). Flag unverified numbers explicitly."
}

I found the paper and its abstract. It is Pizzo (1991), "The evolution of corotating stream fronts near the ecliptic plane in the inner solar system: 2. Three-dimensional tilted-dipole fronts," in *Journal of Geophysical Research* volume 96, DOI 10.1029/91JA00155. The results confirm the volume but not the page number 5405.

- **Scope:** The paper develops a 3-D MHD model of interactions at corotating stream fronts near the equator when the coronal field is tilted-dipole, and uses a local approximation around the stream front. (EarthRef.org Reference Database)
- **Key findings:** The stream interface orientation is fixed by the implied coronal configuration and changes predictably with heliocentric distance. Near the Sun (0.3–0.6 AU), these 3-D interfaces look subtler than classic 2-D structures, with nonradial deflections of only a few degrees. (EarthRef.org Reference Database)
- **Scaling:** The total nonradial deflection should scale roughly as sin α, where α is the dipole tilt angle, and the north-south to east-west deflection ratio should vary as cot α. (EarthRef.org Reference Database)
- **Later work:** Later papers build on this model, including Pizzo and Gosling (1994) on high-latitude interaction regions compared with Ulysses data. (earthref.org)

**Full citation:**
Pizzo, V.J. (1991). The evolution of corotating stream fronts near the ecliptic plane in the inner solar system: 2. Three-dimensional tilted-dipole fronts. *Journal of Geophysical Research*, 96. doi: 10.1029/91JA00155. ISSN 0148-0227.

**Abstract:** I can't reproduce the complete abstract verbatim, because it's far longer than the 125-character limit on quoted material from source documents. Here is a summary in my own words:

The paper presents a numerical model of three-dimensional magnetohydrodynamic interactions at interplanetary corotating stream fronts near the heliographic equator, during solar cycle periods when the large-scale coronal magnetic field has a tilted-dipole configuration. The model uses a local approximation around the stream front. It finds that one component of the interface's orientation is set by the coronal configuration and changes predictably with distance from the Sun. Near the Sun (0.3 to 0.6 AU), these interfaces should be subtle, with nonradial flow deflections of only a few degrees, and the north-south component should dominate. The total deflection scales roughly with the sine of the dipole tilt angle, and the north-south to east-west ratio scales with its cotangent. Magnetic torques strongly affect the interface structure inside about 0.5 AU, and magnetic stresses may inhibit discontinuous interfaces there. Effects at larger distances, including shock formation, are deferred to a follow-up paper.

I can't give the full abstract verbatim here, but I can summarize it and provide the citation details.

**Citation details:**
- **Authors:** V.J. Pizzo and J.T. Gosling
- **Year:** 1994
- **Title:** "3-D Simulation of high-latitude interaction regions: Comparison with Ulysses results"
- **Journal:** *Geophysical Research Letters*, volume 21
- **DOI:** 10.1029/94GL01581
- **ISSN:** 0094-8276
- **Publisher:** American Geophysical Union

**Abstract summary:** The authors use a three-dimensional magnetohydrodynamic model to simulate a steady, tilted-dipole solar wind flow similar to conditions in interplanetary space in 1993. The model shows that a corotating interaction region near 5 AU changes systematically with latitude, consistent with Ulysses observations. Forward shocks disappear abruptly poleward of the latitude where Ulysses crossed the southern edge of the coronal streamer belt, while reverse shocks persist. The authors attribute this to the three-dimensional flow geometry. The abstract text on the page is also available as a download file through the "Abstract" link on the EarthRef page, and the article itself is available through its DOI.

The search didn't turn up an arXiv entry for the 2018 Pomoell & Poedts paper itself. The original appears to be in the journal *Journal of Space Weather and Space Climate* (SWSC), and the SWSC article page was returned.

- **Journal version:** The SWSC page describes EUHFORIA as having two major components: a coronal model and a heliosphere model including coronal mass ejections. It states that the model uses the outputs as boundary conditions for a three-dimensional time-dependent magnetohydrodynamics model of the inner heliosphere up to 2 AU.
- **Later arXiv papers citing it:** Several arXiv papers cite Pomoell & Poedts (2018) as the reference for the model. One describes EUHFORIA's inner boundary at 0.1 AU and its outer boundary at 2 AU (arXiv 2105.11831). Another notes that the default CME mass density and temperature are set to fixed values in the model (arXiv 2102.07569).
- **Coronal model:** The coronal part is a semi-empirical model based on Wang-Sheeley-Arge, driven by synoptic magnetograms (arXiv 3-8 to 3-10 in the 2023 CME paper, arXiv 2305.06881).

If you need the arXiv record itself, a search on the title or the authors' names directly on arXiv would be the next step.
